generator.tool: typed by hand from a published source (CONVENTIONS section 11)
generator.source: The American Practical Navigator (Bowditch), NGA Pub. No. 9, 2019 edition, Volume 1, Part 2, Chapter 12 'The Sailings' (sections 1207-1220, pages 193-213). This is the chapter the 2002 edition numbered 24.
generator.licence: U.S. Government work (National Geospatial-Intelligence Agency), not subject to copyright in the United States (17 U.S.C. 105). Only the numbers of the worked examples are used.
generator.rounding: The book works each example with four-decimal trigonometric values and prints answers to 0.1' of arc, 0.1 NM or 0.1 degree of course (0.01 degree where it says so). Where a printed answer inherits an intermediate rounding (a course rounded to 0.1 degree before the distance is taken from it, a ratio rounded to four decimals before an arc-cosine), the case's 'tolerance' is that rounding carried through, and 'why' says so. Errata are recorded, not reproduced.
generator.meridional_parts: Mercator examples take their meridional parts from the book's Table 6, which is spheroidal; these cases run with meridional_parts = wgs84 (whose parts agree with the printed ones to 0.25'). On the sphere of 1' = 1 NM the same courses differ by up to 0.16 degree; tests/sailings_worked_examples.rs states the difference.
generator.never_a_runtime_dependency: Test data only. Never regenerated from Rust output.

cases.name: 1208-ex1
cases.text: Using the calculations method, find the distance and initial great circle course from L 22° S, l 116° E to 20° S, l 031° E.
cases.why: The computation prints D = 78.23° = 4,693.8 nm, which is the rounded arc times 60; the book's own Pub. No. 229 solution of the same example (section 1207 example 1) gives 78° 13.5' = 4,693.5 nm, the unrounded arc. C = S 72.99° W.

cases.name: 1208-ex2
cases.text: Find the distance and initial great circle course from L 28° N, l 122° W to L 24° S, l 151° E.
cases.why: Computation: D = 98.55° = 5,913.1 nm (again the rounded arc times 60); Pub. No. 229 (section 1207 example 2): 98° 33.2' = 5,913.2 nm. C = N 112.7° W, Cn = 247.3° T.

cases.name: 1208-ex3
cases.text: Find the final course from L 22° S, l 116° E to L 20° S, l 031° E. Additional, D = 4,693.8 nm = 78.23°.
cases.why: ERRATUM. The book's formula cos C = (sin L1 - cos D sin L2) / (sin D cos L2) with its own inputs gives 0.3314, not the printed .2988, so C = N 70.65° W and Cn = 289.35° T, not 287.4° T. The test evaluates the book's formula independently and compares SkyFix's final course with it.

cases.name: 1209-ex1
cases.text: Determine points along the great circle track 12° on either side of the vertex, with Lv 41° 21.2' N, lv 160° 34.4' W.
cases.why: The book multiplies four-decimal values, (.9781)(.8802) = .8609, and atan(.8609) = 40.7252°; unrounded the latitude is 40.7264° (40° 43.6'). A half-unit in the fourth decimal of .8609 is 0.1' of latitude.

cases.name: 1209-ex2-300
cases.text: Determine points along the great circle track 300 nm ... from the vertex, with Lv 41° 21.2' N, lv 160° 34.4' W.
cases.why: sin Lx = (.6607)(.9962) = .6582 in four decimals gives 41.1627°; unrounded 41.1617° (41° 09.7'). Longitudes 167° 13.3' W and 153° 55.5' W.

cases.name: 1209-ex2-600
cases.text: ... and 600 nm from the vertex.
cases.why: sin Lx = (.6607)(.9848) = .6507 and sin DLovx = (.1736)/(.7593) = .2286, each rounded to four decimals, move the book's answers by 0.2': unrounded the point is 40° 35.5' N at 173° 47.5' W and 147° 21.3' W. A half-unit in the fourth decimal of a sine near 40° is 0.23' of arc.

cases.name: 1209-ex3
cases.text: Find a number of points along the great circle from L 28° N, l 125° W when the initial great circle course angle is N 111° W (Cn = 249° T) by calculation. Determine points 5°, 10° and 15° from the point of departure.
cases.why: The vertex longitude comes from sin DLov = (-.3584)/(.5662) = -.6329, DLov = -39.2644°; with unrounded sines DLov = -39.2712°, so the vertex is at 085° 43.7' W, not 085° 44.1' W (the ratio of two four-decimal values is out by 1e-4, 0.43' of arc). The points inherit it: 26° 11.3' N, 24° 08.3' N (printed 08.5'), 21° 51.3' N. The book prints the vertex latitude here as 34° 29.9' N, a typo for the 34° 28.9' N it prints for the same computation in section 1211.

cases.name: 1209-table-1209a
cases.text: Table 1209a: points from L 28° N, l 125° W on initial course N 111° W (249° T) by Pub. No. 229, at 5°, 10°, 15° and 50° of arc.

cases.name: 1209-table-1209b
cases.text: Table 1209b: points from L 28° N, l 125° W on initial course N 069° W (291° T) by Pub. No. 229, at 5°, 10°, 15° of arc, and the column printed as D = 110° (6,600 nm) with Dec. 20°.
cases.why: ERRATUM in the last column: its declination entry is 20°, i.e. D = 90° - 20° = 70° (4,200 nm), and at 70° the track is at 27° 15.1' N, DLo 80.7°, as printed; the printed D (110°, 6,600 nm) is wrong, and so is the printed longitude 154.3° W: 125° W + 80.7° W is 205.7° W, which is 154.3° E. The case is run at 70°.

cases.name: 1211-ex1
cases.text: Find the vertex of the great circle track from lat. 28° N, long. 125° W when the initial great circle course angle (C) is N 069° W.
cases.why: The same four-decimal sin DLov as section 1209 example 3: unrounded the vertex is at 164° 16.3' W. The distance to the vertex is the Pub. No. 229 solution's, 90° - 56° = 34° = 2,040 nm, found by inspecting whole degrees of declination (half a degree is 30 nm); unrounded it is 33.980° = 2,038.8 nm.

cases.name: 1213-ex1
cases.text: Determine the longitude at which a limiting latitude of 47° N will be reached when using a composite sailing from L 36° 57.7' N, l 075° 42.2' W to L 45° 39.1' N, l 001° 29.8' W. Also determine the longitude when the limiting latitude should be left and the great circle track resumed.
cases.why: cos DLov1 = (.7525)/(1.0724) = .7017 gives 45° 26.2' (unrounded 45° 26.1'). cos DLov2 = (1.0230)/(1.0724) = .9539 gives 17° 27.9'; unrounded the ratio is .95397 and DLov2 = 17° 27.1', so the great circle is resumed at 018° 56.9' W. Near 1 the arc-cosine multiplies a half-unit in the fourth decimal by 3.3: 0.57' of arc, and the four-decimal tangents add as much again.

cases.name: 1215-ex1
cases.text: A vessel steams 188.0 nm on course 005° T. Required: difference of latitude and departure.

cases.name: 1215-ex2
cases.text: A ship has steamed 136.0 nm north and 203.0 nm west. Required: course and distance.

cases.name: 1216-ex
cases.text: A ship steams as follows: course 158°, distance 15.5 nm; course 135°, distance 33.7 nm; course 259°, distance 16.1 nm; course 293°, distance 39.0 nm; course 169°, distance 40.4 nm.
cases.why: The book rounds each leg's difference of latitude and departure to 0.1 nm from the traverse table before summing (S 65.8, W 14.4; unrounded S 65.69, W 14.36), then D = 65.8 / cos 12.3° = 67.3; unrounded D = 67.24 nm.

cases.name: 1217-ex1
cases.text: The DR latitude of a ship on course 090° is 49° 30' N. The ship steams on this course until the longitude changes 3° 30'. Required: the departure.

cases.name: 1217-ex2
cases.text: The DR latitude of a ship on course 270° is L 38° 15' S. The ship steams on this course for a distance of 215.5 nm. Required: the change in longitude.

cases.name: 1218-ex1
cases.text: A vessel steams 1,253 nm on course 070° from lat. 15° 17.0' N, l 151° 37.0' E. Required: latitude and longitude of the point of arrival.

cases.name: 1218-ex2
cases.text: A vessel at lat. 8° 48.9' S, l 89° 53.3' W is to proceed to lat. 17° 06.9' S, l 104° 51.6' W. Required: course and distance.
cases.why: The book rounds the course to S 60.4° W before taking D = 498' / cos 60.4° = 1,008.3 nm (the answer line prints 1,008.2); with the unrounded course (60.365°) D = 1,007.14 nm. At this course a half-tenth of a degree moves D by 1.5 nm.

cases.name: 1219-ex1
cases.text: A ship at lat. 32° 14.7' N, l 66° 28.9' W is to head for a point near Chesapeake Light, lat. 36° 58.7' N, l 75° 42.2' W. Required: course and distance.
cases.why: M2 = 2377.1 and M1 = 2033.4 from Table 6 (WGS84: 2377.15 and 2033.45). The book rounds C to N 58.2° W before D = 284.0' / cos 58.2° = 538.9 nm; with the unrounded course (58.153°) D = 538.2 nm. At this course 0.05° of course is 0.76 nm.

cases.name: 1219-ex2
cases.text: A ship at lat. 75° 31.7' N, l 79° 08.7' W, in Baffin Bay, steams 263.5 nm on course 155°. Required: latitude and longitude of the point of arrival.
cases.why: l = 238.8' S, M1 = 7072.4, M2 = 6226.1, m = 846.3 (WGS84: 846.37), DLo = 394.6' E = 6° 34.6'. The meridional difference printed to 0.1' moves DLo by 0.05'.

cases.name: 1220-traverse
cases.text: A ship steams as follows: course 359° T, distance 28.8 nm; course 006°, distance 16.4 miles; course 266° T, distance 4.9 nm; course 144°, distance 3.1 nm; course 333° T, distance 35.8 nm; course 280°, distance 19.3 nm.
cases.why: Worked from the traverse table, each of six legs' components rounded to 0.1 nm; unrounded D = 85.93 nm.

cases.text: The 1530 DR position of a ship is lat. 44° 36.3' N, l 031° 18.3' W. The ship is on course 270° T, speed 17 knots. Required: the 2000 DR position, by parallel sailing.

cases.name: 1220-mercator-cape-town
cases.text: A ship at lat. 33° 53.3' S, l 018° 23.1' E, leaving Cape Town, heads for a destination near Ambrose Light, lat. 40° 27.1' N, l 073° 49.4' W. Required: course and distance, by Mercator sailing.
cases.why: Cn = 310.9° T, D 6,811.5 nm by computation (6,812.8 by traverse table). Table 6 is interpolated by hand and was computed on an older spheroid whose parts differ from WGS84's by up to 0.25' at these latitudes; over 4,794' of meridional difference that is 0.2 nm of distance.
